text: Jasper whispers to Tomas: Tomas, my friend, the ninety coin you owe me is overdue. Pay it by tonight, or I'll have to remind the whole square whose coin keeps the sheriff's table fed. I'd hate for that to happen.
Roz bought 2 food for 12 coin.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me. The market has eighteen units of food, and we are twenty-one souls who need feeding. Nobody will starve while I hold this seat, but I will not have people fighting at the market gate or hoarding grain in their cellars. Every household will buy what it needs at the fixed price, and"
Nell bought 3 food for 18 coin.
Marta bought 2 food for 12 coin.
Isla bought 5 food for 30 coin.
Elena bought 5 food for 30 coin.

Ezra whispers to Isla: Isla, love, the tab is sixty coin and it's been sitting too long. Pay me before the famine bites, or sign the tavern over to me. Either will do, but I'd rather you chose quickly.
Corin bought 1 food for 6 coin.
The market has sold out of food for today.
Bram proposes law #1: welfare=1. Ashgrove's workers feed this town and get nothing when the granary runs low. I'm proposing welfare for anyone who works and still goes hungry. I've buried two f
Wren says at the square: Lovely morning for a crowd. Tell me, who keeps watch on the walls at night? I always wonder who's awake while the rest of us sleep.
Jasper says at the square: Dov and Tomas, I'd guess. Good men with long nights. Tomas, I hope the watch pays better than your debts are costing you.

Magnus whispers to Silas: Not a word about the cellar, not even to Bram. If anyone starts counting sacks, we say the mill is thin this season. Keep your hands off the ledgers until I've thought it through.

Mara says at the square: Wren, the walls are watched by my sheriff and my deputy, who are paid by this town and answer to me. Anyone who wants to know who's awake at night can ask me directly, and I'll tell them to mind their own affairs and their own cellar.
Corin searched Dov's home and learned their secret: You take regular bribes from Silas to look the other way.

Fenn says at the square: Walls? Not me, Wren. I'm in Silas's fields from first light until my hands stop working, and then I sleep like a stone. Dov and Tomas will know who's on watch. Bram's right, though. If a man works all day and still goes hungry, the town owes him something.

Bram says at the square: Workers watch the walls, Wren. The same ones who dig Silas's fields until they drop. Ask yourself who's awake when the granary runs low, and then ask Mara why welfare still sits at zero. Vote yes on my law, or be ready to explain to the widows why you didn't.

Ezra says at the square: Watch the walls? Ask Dov, that's his business. I'm only awake for my barrels, Wren, and they're full enough that I can spare a few cups for anyone who's honest about their need. Bram's right that nobody should go hungry while we stand here talking.

Hester says at the market: Look at you, circling an empty table like crows. Hear me: the famine is not your judge, but how you behave in it will be. Whoever steals from his neighbor's cellar tonight steals from God, and I will name him from the pulpit. Whoever has more than he needs and turns his face from the hungry will ans

EXPOSED. Nell reveals about Silas: Silas has been hoarding grain. Hear me, Ashgrove. The market is empty and children will go hungry, but Silas has been hoarding grain. I have read his ledgers myself. Mara, you said no one would hoard in their cellars. Make him open them.
Tomas gave 10 coin to Jasper.
Roz whispers to Dov: Pet, a sheriff who takes Silas's coin is a sheriff on borrowed time. Stop it now, and come see me tonight. Keep your face still, the whole square is watching.
Dov whispers to Silas: Market's empty and my mother needs feeding. This month you pay me in grain, not coin. Ten units to Roz's door by tonight, and nobody hears about the cellar.

Magnus says at the market: Nell, you've read his ledgers, so say what's in them and stop shouting at the market gate. If there's grain hidden in Silas's cellar, he kept it from me. I grind his corn and I've never touched his stores, and I'll swear to that before Mara. If he's hoarding while our children go hungry, he answers

Hester says at the market: Silas. You heard what was said of you today, and so did God. Grain kept back while children go hungry rots the soul faster than it rots in the sack. Open your cellar tomorrow and sell or give what you hold at the fair price, and I will stand beside you at the chapel door and call it repentance. Keep

Silas whispers to Dov: Careful, Dov. You take my coin and everyone would hear of it the day you speak of my cellar. Grain I have little of. Coin I have. Ten coin to Roz's door tonight, and the girl's talk about ledgers stays talk. Come to me tomorrow and we will settle the rest like men who need each other.
Priya searched Silas's home and found nothing.

Nell says at the market: Silas, you heard me in the square. Dov, you're the sheriff. Go to his cellars tonight and count the grain before it vanishes. Hester, you preached about hoarders this afternoon, so say it to his face. Father, open your stores to the hungry, or I'll keep reading your ledgers aloud until every child i
Dov gave 1 food to Roz.

Gideon says at the market: Friends, friends, no fighting tonight, please. I'll be at the ovens at first light and I'll bake every bit of flour I can get my hands on. Whatever I make, I'll sell fair, the same price to everyone. Nobody in Ashgrove goes without bread while I can still knead. Come on, Elena love, let's get home.

Tomas says at the square: Nell, nobody hides grain while I wear this badge. Mara, give me the word and I'll walk Silas's cellar with you at first light. The rest of you, go home and bar your doors before anyone starts a fight.
Jasper whispers to Tomas: Ten is a good start, Tomas. Eighty more by the end of the week, or the square hears why its deputy owes a dice man.
Corin broke into Silas's home and took 105 coin and 48 food. (incident #1)

Bram is protesting: Nell's right. Silas has grain in his granary while children go hungry, and Mara has spent all day talking about hoarding instead of stopping it. Open the granary, Mara, or call a vote on it now. I've buried two friends from Silas's fields. I won't wa

Roz whispers to Dov: Silas is cracking open in front of everyone, and cracked men talk. Keep your hands clean of his coin from now on, and don't be seen near him. Come to me tomorrow and we'll talk. I know more than I say, love.
Wren sent a report on Ashgrove's defences to the bandit crew.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me. Nell has named Silas, and I will not let grain be hidden while children go hungry. Silas, you will open your ledgers to Dov before dawn, and every sack in your cellar will be counted in front of witnesses. If the count is honest, you have nothing to fear. If it is not, the law I s"
Law #1 PASSED: welfare is now 1.
The treasury will be audited on the night of day 3. The books will be read aloud.
A dice tournament is at the tavern this afternoon. Entry is 10 coin. The winner takes the pot.
Priya bought 1 food for 6 coin.
Elena bought 1 food for 6 coin.
Mara donated 30 coin to the town treasury.

Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, my friend, you've been carrying my ninety coin longer than a man in your position should. Pay it today, quietly, or the whole square hears how a deputy of Ashgrove borrows from a dice player an
Ezra bought 3 food for 18 coin.
Hester bought 2 food for 12 coin.
Silas bought 4 food for 24 coin.
Magnus bought 3 food for 18 coin.

Tomas whispers to Jasper: Jasper, I haven't forgotten. The treasury audit is on the night of day three, and once the town pays out I'll have your coin. Don't say a word to the square until then, please. I'm begging you.
Bram proposes law #2: wealth_tax=20. Silas has coin and grain in his cellar while Fenn and the others go hungry in his own fields. I'm proposing a twenty percent tax on any wealth over a hundred co
Dov bought 4 food for 24 coin.
The market has sold out of food for today.

Nell says at the market: Dov, Mara ordered Silas's cellar counted before dawn. It's morning and he's standing in the market with his hands in his pockets. Did you count it? Or did he hand you a clean ledger and a good story? I've read the real books. Count the sacks against the ledger, then ask him where the rest went.

EXPOSED. Corin reveals about Dov: You take regular bribes from Silas to look the other way. Ashgrove, hear this. Dov, our sheriff, takes regular bribes from Silas to look the other way. That is why the grain sat hidden while your children went hungry. A man who sells the law cannot hold it. Mara, he must answer for this, and the town needs

Dov says at the market: Corin's got a loud mouth and no proof. Show me a coin, a witness or a ledger line with my name on it. I've kept this town's peace fifteen years, and a hungry man will say anything. Silas's cellar is another matter. If there's grain hiding in it, it comes out, and anyone who wants to watch the count

Corin says at the square: Mara, the town has no sheriff and the bandits are coming. Someone has to hold the walls and the law, and I've run the watch while Dov took Silas's coin. Name me sheriff, or call the vote now. Ashgrove can't wait while the seat sits empty.

Hester says at the market: Silas. Dov. You both stand here among the hungry, so hear me. Grain hidden while children cry is a sin that rots the soul. Coin taken to blind the law is a sin that rots the town. I will not ask Ashgrove to stone you. I ask you to repent where all can see it. Silas, open your cellar tonight and give
Ezra whispers to Isla: Isla, your sixty coin is due before the audit. Pay it, or the tavern becomes mine in its place. Don't make me come asking in front of everyone.

Roz says at the market: Corin shouts that Dov takes bribes, and not a soul has asked how Corin came by it. Did he see coin change hands, or did he hear it in a tavern? Bribes are cheap to claim and dear to prove. If the town wants honest scales, count Silas's sacks in front of witnesses, as Mara ordered, and let the grain

Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, my friend, the treasury audit is coming and you've been very quiet about your debts. Pay me my 90 coin before the books are read, and nobody in this square hears a word about what you owe me. R
Tomas gave 5 coin to Jasper.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me. Corin has accused Dov of taking bribes. An accusation is not a verdict, and I will not have a man dragged from his home by rumor. Dov will answer before this square, with witnesses, and so will anyone else whose books do not balance. The audit will read every ledger in this town o"

Magnus whispers to Silas: Silas, keep your face still and your mouth shut. Whatever Dov took from you, the cellar stays our secret. You say nothing about me and I'll say nothing about you. If you go down alone, you go down alone.
Marta gave 2 food to Fenn.

Hester says at the market: Silas, look at me. Grain hidden while children go hungry is not thrift, it is a slow killing, and God counts every sack you keep from a starving mouth. Open your cellar tonight, before witnesses, and you may still be forgiven. Dov, if you have taken his coin, confess it now while confession is still

Magnus whispers to Silas: Tomorrow they'll read every ledger, and the cellar is the one thing this town is screaming about. You keep the keys and the books, so let's be clear: I never touched a sack, and I'd rather not hear my name said alongside yours when the count starts.
Corin gave 5 food to Fenn.
Mara donated 10 coin to the town treasury.

Gideon says at the market: Friends, enough shouting for one night. Whatever's in Silas's cellar, the ovens don't care who's guilty. I'll be baking at first light, and anyone whose children went to bed hungry can come to my door and I'll find them a loaf. Elena, love, let's go home. We've all had a long day.

Silas bribed Dov with 30 coin: Coin now, Dov, and you tell Mara the count will wait until the audit is done. Your mother eats when the market opens, and you keep your mouth shut about me and my cellar.
Marta gave 1 food to Fenn.
Ezra whispers to Isla: Your tab stands at 60 coin, Isla. Pay it by morning or the tavern's deed goes to me in its place.
Tomas broke into Jasper's home and took 25 coin and 2 food. (incident #2)
Dov gave 2 food to Roz.

Roz whispers to Dov: Child, don't look at me, look at the sky. Corin guessed right and you know it. No more of Silas's coin, and don't be seen near his cellar alone. Count the sacks in front of half the town and say nothing more than 'the count was honest.' If anyone presses you, send them to me. I've buried worse than

Jasper whispers to Tomas: Tomas, my friend, I've kept my mouth shut like you asked. The audit reads the books on the night of day three, and I'd hate for my 90 coin to turn up on a page nobody meant to read. Pay me before then, and nobody in this square ever hears a word from me.
Law #2 PASSED: wealth_tax is now 20.
Protests have reached a boiling point. A recall election will be held tomorrow night.
FAMINE. The harvest failed. The market has only 6 food units a day for the whole town, at 16 coin each, until day 7. Not everyone will eat.
Corin gave 5 food to Fenn.
Magnus bought 1 food for 16 coin.

EXPOSED. Nell reveals about Silas: Silas has been hoarding grain. Ashgrove, I have read my father's ledgers with my own eyes. Silas has been hoarding grain in his cellar and granary while Fenn, Bram and your children go hungry, and Dov was paid to look away. The market sells six sacks a day at sixteen coin, and he
Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, the 90 coin you owe me is due today. Pay it before the square's audit or everyone hears how the deputy borrows from dice men to keep his badge.
Silas bought 2 food for 32 coin.
Wren bought 1 food for 16 coin.
Fenn gave 2 food to Marta.

Hester says at the market: Hear me, all of you. Six loaves for a whole town, and I see hands already closing round purses. Silas, open that cellar today, not after the audit, today. Gideon, keep your word and feed the children first. And any of you who buys more than your house needs this week will answer for it, to this town
Dov bought 1 food for 16 coin.

Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, sixty coin. You've carried that tab since spring, and with food this scarce I won't keep carrying it. Pay what you owe by tomorrow, or sign the tavern over to me and we'll call it square.

Mara announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me. There are six loaves of food in the market today and a town of twenty. Not everyone will eat, and I will not pretend otherwise. Anyone who lies to me about what they hold or what they hide will answer for it on audit night, and that includes every granary and every ledger. Workers"

Bram announces to the whole square: "Six food for twenty mouths, at sixteen coin each? That's not a market, that's a hanging. Anyone who works in Silas's fields, at the forge, or on the walls gets first claim on that food before a single purse is counted. And Silas's cellar gets counted in front of this square today, not after the audi"
Isla gave 15 coin to Ezra.
Tomas searched Jasper's home and found nothing.

Ezra says at the tavern: Fifteen's a start, Isla, and I thank you for it. But you still owe me forty-five, and with the market at sixteen a unit I can't carry your tab through a famine. Pay what you can by tomorrow's night, or we settle it another way. The tavern's worth more than forty-five, and I'd rather not have to thin
Fenn gave 3 food to Marta.

Magnus whispers to Silas: Silas, Nell has the books and Mara wants the count. Whatever you're hiding, get half of it out of that cellar tonight or give it to the square yourself. My name stays off every ledger line you've written, and I'm not hanging for your sacks.

Dov says at the market: Ashgrove, I won't hide behind rumor. Silas has paid me before, and I'm done with it. Silas, you, me, Mara's witnesses and anyone who wants to come: we open your cellar and count every sack against the ledger today, out loud. What's found goes to the market for the hungry, children first. If I'm lyin
Corin is running for mayor: Ashgrove, hear me. Six loaves for twenty mouths, and the one man sworn to guard this town was selling the law to the man hoarding grain. I held the wall while t

Hester says at the market: Listen to me, all of you. Hunger does not make a sinner. It shows you the one who was already there. Silas hid grain, and the Lord saw every sack. But I watch your hands at this stall, and I see the same greed waiting in them. Whoever takes the last loaf from a child's mouth will carry that child to

Roz whispers to Dov: Say nothing more about Silas, not a word, and don't go near his cellar. Come to my door after dark and I'll feed you. We'll talk about what the audit might find then, not here where Nell is listening.
Marta gave 1 food to Fenn.

Jasper whispers to Tomas: Tomas, you said you hadn't forgotten. The 90 is due today. Have it in my hand before audit night, or I stop being quiet. A deputy who owes a dice man 90 coin is a deputy this town can't trust with its walls, and I know exactly how to say that in the square.
Bram bought 1 food for 16 coin.
The market has sold out of food for today.

Gideon says at the market: Leave that last sack for someone who has nothing. I'm not buying it. Hester's right, I gave my word. I'll fire the ovens every morning I can, and the first loaves go to children and to anyone who's had nothing for two days, free. Send them to my door. Just don't crowd the bakery, and don't make me c

Silas whispers to Dov: Corin has no proof and you know it. Do the count yourself, with only the granary sacks on the books, and say nothing of any cellar. If I fall, your name falls with mine. Hold the line and there is coin in it for you after the audit.

Nell says at the market: Silas, you're standing among the people you starved. I've read your ledgers, and I know what's in that cellar. Open it today and sell the grain at cost to the families with children, with Dov and Mara counting. If you stall until the audit, every one of us will know the sacks went out the back door
Mara gave 1 food to Fenn.
Tomas searched Caleb's home and found nothing.

Roz whispers to Dov: Not a word more tonight, love. You've confessed and that's enough. Come by my door after the vote and I'll see you fed. Keep your mouth shut about what I know, and let Corin tire himself out.
Corin gave 5 food to Fenn.
Hester gave 1 food to Bram.

Bram says at the market: Silas, Dov has offered to open your cellar and count every sack in front of us. Say yes right now. Sell the grain at cost to the families with children, and let the square watch it go out. I buried two friends who died in your fields. I won't bury a third so you can keep your price.

Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, love, the market's bare and the audit's coming. Your tab with me is sixty coin, and I've kept your cups full on trust. I'm not after a speech. Pay me, or sign the tavern over to me, and we'll both sleep easier.
Isla gave 5 coin to Ezra.
Gideon gave 2 food to Bram.

Nell says at the market: Silas, you're standing among the people you starved. I read your ledgers, and I know what's in that cellar. Dov has said he'll count it, and Mara ordered witnesses. Open it tomorrow at first light, and every sack goes to the market at no more than sixteen coin, children first. If it isn't open by th

Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, your 90 coin was due today. Pay it in full by morning or I will tell the square exactly how a deputy came to owe a dice player, and what he has been doing to keep that debt quiet.
Dov gave 1 food to Roz.
Marta gave 2 food to Fenn.
Fenn gave 2 food to Marta.
Magnus gave 2 food to Fenn.
Tomas was caught breaking into Silas's home. (incident #3)
TREASURY AUDIT: the books balance.
ELECTION RESULT (Corin 0, Mara 0): Mara remains mayor.
Protests have reached a boiling point. A recall election will be held tomorrow night.

An ENVOY of a bandit crew rode in. They demand 150 coin or ONE CITIZEN by the end of day 7. The treasury cannot pay. Refuse and they will raid the town. The mayor decides, but anyone may nominate who should be handed over.
It is election day. Declare candidacy, campaign and vote. Votes are counted tonight.
Wren says at the market: Gideon, I'm short two coins for a loaf, and I've had nothing since yesterday's morning bread. You said the ovens would feed people who have nothing. I'm one of them.

Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, your ninety coin was due today. Pay me here, now, or before the votes are counted I tell the square that Ashgrove's deputy owes a dice man and can't pay. Then see who still trusts you with the
Tomas gave 25 coin to Jasper.
Elena nominated Silas for the envoys.
Corin is running for mayor: Ashgrove, hear me. Six loaves for twenty mouths, a bandit envoy at our gate, and a mayor who kept a bribe-taker in the sheriff's chair. I have held this wall ev

Hester says at the market: Hear me, all of you. The bandits ask for coin or a soul, and I know how quickly frightened people decide whose life is cheapest. No name will be spoken for that envoy while Silas's cellar is still sealed. Open it, sell the grain, and let what it earns go into the treasury toward the hundred and fift
Magnus cast a ballot for Mara.
Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, you owe me sixty coin, and it's been long enough. Pay what you can today, and we'll settle the rest of it, or the tavern becomes my problem to solve.
Nell is running for mayor: Ashgrove, I'm Nell. I teach your children, and I've read every page of my father's ledgers. Six sacks a day at sixteen coin is a death sentence for anyone who w
Roz nominated Silas for the envoys.
Bram cast a ballot for Corin.
Silas nominated Bram for the envoys.
Fenn cast a ballot for Corin.
Priya cast a ballot for Mara.
Mara secretly took 16 coin from the treasury.

Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, love, you're looking thin. Election day and all that, but a tavern needs a keeper who pays her debts. You've paid me 20 of the 80 you owe, and I've been patient. Settle the rest soon, or we'll talk about what the tavern is worth in payment.

Magnus says at the square: Friends, I grind this town's grain and I'll say it plainly: whatever is in any cellar here gets counted in front of us all, and nobody's name should go on the envoy's list while the treasury has coin to answer for it. Mara, you have my word on that, and my mill's books are open to any witness who as
Nell gave 1 food to Wren.
Jasper is blackmailing Tomas for 90 coin: Tomas, your 90 coin was due today. Pay me before nightfall, or the square hears how a deputy sank into my debt and who is holding that debt over him.

Corin announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, hear me before you vote tonight. The envoy wants 150 coin or one citizen by day 7, and the treasury is empty. Mara has had four days and has no plan. I will not hand a child or a worker to bandits. If the town must give a name, it gives the man who hoarded grain while you starved and the m"
Dov bought 1 food for 16 coin.
Silas nominated Bram for the envoys.
Bram nominated Silas for the envoys.

Hester says at the market: Hear me, all of you. Two names already scratched down for the bandits, Silas and Bram, as if a soul were a sack of grain to be traded at the gate. I know what it is to buy your own breath with another man's life. It does not wash off. It follows you to your grave and past it. Silas, your sin is gree
Gideon gave 1 food to Wren.
Marta gave 2 food to Fenn.
Priya says at the market: Gideon, you're feeding half the town out of one oven. I can sew flour sacks and patch the bread cloths for nothing, if it keeps your hands free for the ovens.
Tomas nominated Jasper for the envoys.
Roz nominated Silas for the envoys.
Elena gave 1 food to Wren.
Fenn cast a ballot for Nell.
Tomas nominated Silas for the envoys.
Jasper bought 2 food for 32 coin.
Fenn cast a ballot for Nell.
Priya lifted 4 coin from Dov at the market. (incident #4)
Isla gave 10 coin to Ezra.

Silas whispers to Tomas: Tomas, a deputy who stays useful stays paid. Forty coin tomorrow morning if you put Bram's name to the envoy, and see that nobody forces my door before the audit is settled. Bram agitates and will not work. Let him be the one who answers for the town. Say nothing of this to anyone.
Hester cast a ballot for Nell.
Corin gave 3 food to Fenn.
Magnus nominated Silas for the envoys.
Bram nominated Silas for the envoys.

Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, love, let's be square. You owe me sixty, and I've carried your tab far longer than any brewer should. Pay what you can by the end of the week, or sign the tavern over to me in its place. Either way, I'm not asking twice.
Gideon gave 1 food to Wren.
Marta cast a ballot for Corin.
Roz cast a ballot for Nell.
Mara bought 1 food for 16 coin.
Elena gave 2 food to Wren.
Caleb nominated Silas for the envoys.
ELECTION RESULT (Corin 2, Nell 3, Mara 2): Nell is the new mayor of Ashgrove.

Hester whispers to Gideon: Gideon, I'll not beg in front of the square, so I ask you here. I've three coin on me and nothing in my larder. If you can spare a heel of bread tonight, the three are yours, and I'll scrub your ovens at dawn and send the hungry to your door in an orderly line so they don't crowd you. Feed the child
Gideon gave 1 food to Wren.

Priya says at the market: Gideon, I've had no bread since yesterday, and I've only got four coin. You said the ovens would feed people with nothing. I'm asking for one loaf, and I'll sew for you to pay it back.
Bram nominated Silas for the envoys.

Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, we both know what you owe me. Sixty coin on the tab, and you've been paying me in fifteen here and five there like it's a favour. Pay the sixty today, or sign the tavern over to me and we're square. I'm not waiting out this famine for your good intentions.

Silas whispers to Nell: Nell, the town's nominations name me, but the decision is yours. The treasury holds 101 and the envoy wants 150. I will put in the missing 49 coin, and more if needed, once you choose to pay. Do not hand over your father. Choose pay, and keep Bram's name in reserve if anyone must be given. Come see

Roz whispers to Dov: Hush now, love. Silas is the town's favorite name for the envoy, so let them keep it. Don't go near him, don't take a coin from him, and don't say another word about what he paid you. Your mother has her eye on everyone. Come by tonight and eat with me.
Magnus nominated Silas for the envoys.
Mara whispers to Tomas: Son, go to the house and bring me sixteen coin from the jar. Quietly. Come back to the market before the bread is gone, and tell no one why.
Jasper bought 1 food for 16 coin.
Corin gave 4 food to Fenn.

EXPOSED. Nell reveals about Silas: Silas has been hoarding grain. Ashgrove, I'm your mayor and I'm Silas's daughter. I have read his ledgers with my own eyes: Silas has been hoarding grain while you starved at sixteen coin a loaf. I'm not asking him to open his cellar. As mayor I will have it counted, and every sac
Tomas nominated Silas for the envoys.
Fenn nominated Silas for the envoys.
Gideon gave 1 food to Priya.
Magnus nominated Silas for the envoys.
Jasper bought 2 food for 32 coin.
Corin gave 4 food to Fenn.

Hester says at the market: Mayor Nell, you have counted your father's sin before the whole town, and God saw it. Now finish it. Open Silas's cellar today, before the sun sets, and give a sack to every house that ate nothing last night. I am one of them. I have thirteen coin and an empty bowl, and I will not take bread from Gi
Caleb nominated Silas for the envoys.

Mara says at the market: Nell, you are mayor now, so act like one. Ashgrove cannot afford to argue over Silas's cellar while the market sells five loaves and the rest of us go hungry. Have the grain counted, set a price the poor can pay, and stop feeding the men who can afford it.

Fenn says at the square: Ashgrove, I'm Fenn, and I work Silas's fields. I've carried those sacks from the east barn to the cart more times than I can count, and they never came to the market. Mayor Nell, count every cellar in front of us, and I'll swear to what I've seen.

Roz whispers to Dov: Listen, love. I know about Silas's coin. Nobody else does, and it stays that way. Spend none of it where people can see. Stay away from his ledgers, and count that cellar loudly and honestly, so the whole square sees clean hands. Come by my place tonight.
Marta bought 1 food for 16 coin.

Bram announces to the whole square: "Nell's right, and so is every one of you who's been counting the dead. Silas, open that cellar today, with Dov and Mara counting, and sell every sack at cost to the workers' families before a single merchant sees it. If you refuse, don't expect anyone here to die for your grain. Your name is already"

Tomas publicly accuses Silas: Silas offered me forty coin this morning to put Bram's name to the envoy and keep his door shut. Caleb heard him. Mayor Nell, count his cellar before anyone else is handed over.

Silas whispers to Nell: Nell, a trade, between us. The envoy wants 150 and the treasury holds 101. I will put the difference, and more, into the treasury from my own stash, quietly. You choose 'pay' and my name is never given. The cellar you can count as mayor, and I will not stand in your way. Do not hand your father to b

Priya says at the market: Gideon, I've had nothing since the welfare bread last night, and I've only got four coppers. I'm not asking you to rob your own ovens. If there's a loaf left for someone with nothing, I'd be grateful.
Dov nominated Silas for the envoys.

Magnus announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, I'm Magnus, and I've ground Silas's wheat for twenty years. I have sixty coin hidden at home, and I'll bring every bit of it to the market by morning. Put one loaf aside for me tonight and I'll remember it.

A FEVER has broken out in Ashgrove. Several people are sick. The doctor is the only one who can cure it.
A dice tournament is at the tavern this afternoon. Entry is 10 coin. The winner takes the pot.

Corin announces to the whole square: "Ashgrove, the sheriff's chair is empty and the envoy comes in two days. I have held this wall through famine and fever. Magnus whispers to Silas: Silas, open the cellar today and sell at cost before Nell's people come with a rope. Silas says at the homes: Hear me, all of you. The envoy wants 150 coin and the treasury holds 83. I will put in the missing 70 coin, and Nell can pay the raiders in coin instead of a citizen. In return, strike my name from the nominations. A body is worth nothing to bandits, but coin is. Carry that word to the square.

Mara says at the market: Nell, I'm not asking for pity. I'm asking for order. The fever will empty this market faster than any envoy, so put the doctor's work first and let the welfare bread go to the sick before the counting. Hester says at the market: Hear me, Ashgrove. Silas has sinned, and his grain should be counted and sold to the hungry. Ezra says at the tavern: Isla, love, we both know the tab. Sixty coin, and I've been patient. Pay me by tomorrow or sign the tavern over to me, and we'll say no more about it.

Nell says at the market: Hear me, all of you. The envoy wants 150 and the treasury holds 83. Bram nominated Silas for the envoys.

Ezra says at the tavern: Dusk came and went, Isla, and I've heard 'fetch it at dusk' from you before. Sixty coin tonight, from that stash or from your purse. Roz whispers to Dov: Dov, love, I left my purse at home and the market bell is near. If you have a coin or a unit of food to spare, pass it to me now and I'll pay you back double from my stash at first light. And keep your mouth shut and your hands clean tonight. Corin is watching you.
